title: Devotion and an empty stomach
odia:
ଠକ ଠକ ମାଳି ଭଜନ ଟାଣ
ଭୋକ କଲା ଭାତ ପାଖକୁ ଆଣ |
literal_meaning: “Thaka thaka Mali, bhajana tana”; when hunger comes, bring the rice near. (The opening phrase is retained in transliteration because its precise literal force remains uncertain.)
explanation: The verse sets a loud display of devotion beside an ordinary appetite. It can be read as a jab at performance that conceals self-interest, though the source gives no separate explanation.
meaning_odia: ଜୋର୍ ଭଜନର ଦେଖାଣି ସହ ଭୋକ ଲାଗିଲେ ଭାତ ଖୋଜିବାର ସାଧାରଣ ଆବଶ୍ୟକତାକୁ ପାଖାପାଖି ରଖାଯାଇଛି। ଏଥିରେ ଭକ୍ତିର ପ୍ରଦର୍ଶନ ପଛରେ ନିଜ ସ୍ୱାର୍ଥ ଲୁଚିଥିବାକୁ ଟିପ୍ପଣୀ କରାଯାଉଥିବା ପରି ପଢ଼ିହେବ। ଉତ୍ସରେ ଅଲଗା ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ନଥିବାରୁ ଏହି ପାଠ ସୀମିତ; ଭୋକ ଲାଗିବା ନିଜେ କପଟ ଭକ୍ତିର ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।
usage_example: A fictional character makes a grand show of sacrifice but promptly insists on a special meal. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: ମାଳି remains a source label, not a judgment about a caste or occupation. Neither hunger nor devotional singing is itself treated as proof of hypocrisy. The opening ଠକ ଠକ and ଭଜନ ଟାଣ are not given a definite literal gloss; the interpretation remains provisional.
